reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant' with no redline and no comment, which is the expected output shape for a compliant finding; the rendered redline is identical to the originals, so no unnecessary edit was introduced.

The cited paragraphs (§5.a fees, §6 documentation/disputes, §8.f spamming) contain no audit, inspection or records-examination right running against Client and no vendor access to Client systems — the absence of any audit obligation is better than the playbook's preferred position, so no negotiation issue arises.
The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is explained by the total absence of an audit clause rather than by a permissive one; it is not evidence of a missed deviation.

Rationale correctly notes §6 and §2.e as Client-favourable and flags §8.f technical mechanisms as an acceptable-use enforcement measure on TrueLink's own Interface, not an audit of Client records/systems — an accurate distinction that avoids double-flagging under this rule.
